title: Startup Strategy and Scaling
content: Host: Let's talk about startup growth strategies. What's your philosophy? [00:15] Guest: I think there are three critical phases. First, product-market fit. You must solve a real problem that people want to pay for. Second, repeatable growth. Once you find what works, you scale it. Third, organizational excellence. [01:30] Host: How do you achieve product-market fit? [01:45] Guest: Talk to customers obsessively. Most founders build what they think customers want. That's wrong. You should spend 80% of your time talking to potential users. Ask what problems they face. Listen to their frustrations. [03:00] Host: And if you don't find fit? [03:15] Guest: You pivot. But pivoting is expensive. That's why early validation is critical. Before you build, validate. Before you scale, validate. [04:30] Host: What about competition? [04:45] Guest: Competition is actually a good sign. It means there's a market. Worry when you have zero competition. That usually means the problem isn't worth solving. Your job isn't to avoid competition. It's to be better or different. [06:00] Host: Any advice for early stage founders? [06:15] Guest: Focus on retention, not vanity metrics. Growth that doesn't retain is just waste. If 90% of users leave after day one, growing isn't helping. Secondly, hire slowly. Bad hires are expensive. Third, don't run out of money. This is obvious but so many founders ignore it. Raise capital when you're strong, not when you're desperate.
